newsitem.title: INDIA: India lawmakers slam government "sellout" to WTO.
newsitem.headline: India lawmakers slam government "sellout" to WTO.

text.p: Irate lawmakers demanded a government statement on India's stance at world trade talks and forced the abrupt adjournment of both houses of parliament on Friday.

Members hit out at Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's minority coalition, saying the government had caved in to Western pressure over the sensitive issue of labour standards at this week's meeting of the World Trade Organisation in Singapore.
The critics included members of Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's 13-party United Front alliance.
"It is a sellout to the multinationals. We have caved in to a conspiracy against our sovereignty," a spokeswoman for the opposition Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) said.
"Our total exports will collapse as a result of the agreement," Sushma Swaraj told Reuters.
She was referring to a clause on labour standards which some Asian countries described as a victory for developing countries.
"By putting the clause in the WTO, we have opened up the way for its future misuse," she said.
The view was echoed by her communist rivals.

"The agreement goes against the prime minister's commitment that no decision on substantive issues would be endorsed without consulting all the parties in the government," communist deputy Ashok Mitra said.
"It has now been agreed that the WTO would be the drill master for enforcing labour standards," Mitra said.
There was no official comment from Deve Gowda's own Janata Dal party, but one deputy voiced some fears.

"When foreign guidance takes a stranglehold on issues concerning our nation, it is a serious matter," Janata Dal deputy and party general secretary Wasim Ahmed told Reuters. "Nothing should be done to compromise our sovereignty."
"It is a black day for India," news agencies quoted BJP leader Atal Bihari Vajpayee as saying.
The speaker of the lower house, P.A. Sangma, demanded full details from the government on negotiations on labour standards and investment before India signed the WTO declaration in Singapore.
Newspapers said India had softened its stance at the Singapore meeting over labour standards and investment.
India had opposed linking trade and labour, arguing that rich nations aimed to erect trade barriers in the name of labour standards to protect their industries.
"Things have changed and things are changing," the Press Trust of India (PTI) quoted Sangma as saying.

"We have surrendered to U.S. pressure at the cost of our sovereignty," PTI quoted Rupchand Pal of the Communist Party of India-Marxist (CPI-M) as saying. The CPI-M supports Deve Gowda's centre-left coalition but is not in the government.

PTI quoted Finance Minister P. Chidambaram as saying the "situation (in Singapore) is evolving" but "members will be fully satisfied that the position taken by India is fully consistent with its stated position".
Ministers and officials from 128 countries adopted a final declaration at the end of the five-day WTO conference on Friday.
On the contentious labour issue, they declared a renewed "commitment to the observance of internationally recognised core labour standards".
But they said the United Nations' International Labour Organisation was the "competent body to set a deal on these standards", which could not be used for protectionist purposes.
